samples.summary: Merge-layout changes are not fully invalidated: covered srefs of deleted/created merges are omitted from `changedSrefs`, leaving stale dependant values
samples.evidence:
In the new merge pass, the only srefs added to `changedSrefs` are the dest cells that actually had a cell object (`if (!cell) continue;` at line 2386, before `changedSrefs.add(sref)` at 2392). Nothing adds the covered srefs of a merge whose *aliasing* changed. Two concrete stale-value paths:

(a) Deleted destination merge, no moved merge. Setup: A1='10', B1 empty, A3='20', merge A3:B3, and D1='=B3' (displays 20 through the merge alias, since `fetchGridByReferences` resolves local refs via `normalizeRefToAnchor`, sheet.ts:2699). Move A1:B1 → A3. `overwrittenMerges=[A3:B3]` (fully inside destRange) is deleted at 2366-2367, `movedMerges` is empty so the clearing loop never runs. `changedSrefs` = {A3 (movedGrid), A1, B1 (source clear)} — B3 is absent. `expandChangedSrefsWithMergeAliases` therefore never yields B3, `buildDependantsMap` never reaches D1, and D1 keeps the stale 20 although B3 is now an independent empty cell.

(b) Newly created destination merge over an empty source. Setup: merge A1:B1 with no value, A3='20', B3 empty, D1='=B3' (empty). Move A1:B1 → A3. `movedGrid` is empty, so the new merge A3:B3 is created but the covered cell B3 has no stored cell (`if (!cell) continue;`) and is not added to `changedSrefs`; B3 now aliases to A3='20' but D1 is never recalculated.

Compare `unmergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4351-4356) and `mergeSelection` (4299-4302), which deliberately add *every* covered sref of every affected merge to `changedSrefs` precisely because aliasing changed. The move path only adds cells it happened to write or delete.

samples.summary: New destination-clearing loop deletes spill ghost cells and spill anchors without the spill handling every other clear path performs
samples.evidence: Lines 2382-2393 fetch each destination cell covered by the moved merge and unconditionally `store.delete(ref)` (or rewrite it as `{s: cell.s}`, which drops `spillAnchor`/`spillRows`/`spillCols`). Every neighbouring clear path guards this: the source-clearing loop 12 lines above skips ghosts (`if (sourceCell?.spillAnchor) continue;`, line 2351), as do lines 2201 and 2564, and `removeData` (1117-1140) explicitly deletes an anchor's ghosts and clears spill blockers before removing a spill anchor. Deleting a ghost here leaves the owning anchor's spill array with a hole (nothing queues that anchor for recalculation), and deleting a spill anchor at the destination leaves its ghost cells outside the merge as orphans.

samples.summary: Merge-related rejections are silent no-ops with no signal to the caller or the view
samples.evidence: Both new guards (`return;` at 2295 and 2302) abort the move with no return value and no state change, and `moveRangeTo` returns `Promise<void>`. The only caller, packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:4310, awaits it and then unconditionally clears the drag preview and re-renders, so a drag that is refused (e.g. dropping a single cell onto the anchor of a 1x2 merge, which makes the dest merge not `isRangeInRange(destRange)`) looks to the user like the drop was lost. Existing merge-aware operations return a boolean (`mergeSelection`/`unmergeSelection`) so callers can react; this one cannot be distinguished from a successful move.

samples.summary: Destination cells not present in `movedGrid` are still never cleared, which now interacts badly with merge deletion
samples.evidence: `setGrid(movedGrid)` only writes cells that existed in the source; nothing in `moveRangeTo` clears destination cells whose source counterpart was empty (contrast the new merge-specific clearing at 2382-2393, which does exactly that but only for cells covered by a moved merge). With the new code an overwritten destination merge can be dropped while its anchor's old value survives — e.g. source A1 empty / B1='10' moved onto merge A3:B3 with A3='20' leaves A3='20' unmerged next to the moved B3='10'. Pre-existing gap, but the merge deletion added here makes the leftover visible as a distinct cell rather than merged content.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: in moveRangeTo, `changedSrefs` is fed only by movedGrid srefs (sheet.ts:2341-2343), cleared source cells (2346-2356), and covered cells of newly created merges that already had a stored cell object (2382-2393; `if (!cell) continue;` at 2386 skips the `changedSrefs.add(sref)` at 2392). The `overwrittenMerges` deletion loop (2365-2368) adds nothing at all, so covered srefs whose aliasing changed are never invalidated. `expandChangedSrefsWithMergeAliases` (867-882) runs after `rebuildMergeCoverMap()` (2395) and therefore cannot recover a deleted merge's members, and it only expands srefs already in the set. Dependant edges are keyed by the raw reference text, not the merge anchor (MemStore.buildDependantsMap memory.ts:328-340; YorkieStore.buildDependantsMap yorkie-store.ts:571-592), and `calculate` seeds its traversal solely from the passed refs (calculator.ts:41-46), so a formula `=B3` is unreachable unless `B3` itself is seeded. Stored values are rendered without re-evaluation (toDisplayString sheet.ts:1002-1010), so the stale value persists visibly. I searched for a compensating invalidation elsewhere and found none: no recalculateAllFormulaCells call in this path (used only at 1308/1478/3444), redirectFormulasForCut only recalcs cells whose own formula text changed (2440-2462), store setMerge/deleteMerge have no recalc side effect (memory.ts:459-465, yorkie-store.ts:948-975), endBatch merely flushes (yorkie-store.ts:1163+), and the sole caller only re-renders (view/worksheet.ts:4310). Both described scenarios (deleted destination merge; new merge over an empty covered dest cell) are reachable. Real correctness bug (stale dependant values), major.
